title: Valmiki Ramayana — Yuddha Kanda
source_owner: Ralph T. H. Griffith translation (1870-1874) via Project Gutenberg; Sanskrit companion-only
revision_note: P1 Starter canonical ingestion per RAMAYANA_CANONICAL_SOURCE_PLAN.md Stage 2: Griffith public domain translation, Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
सकृदेव प्रपन्नाय तवास्मीति च याचते ।
अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो ददाम्येतद् व्रतं मम ॥
content.transliteration:
sakṛdeva prapannāya tavāsmīti ca yācate |
abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo dadāmyetad vrataṃ mama ||
content.text: To anyone who surrenders to me even once and declares 'I am yours', I grant freedom from fear to all beings. This is my solemn vow.
content.translation: To anyone who surrenders to me even once and declares 'I am yours', I grant freedom from fear to all beings. This is my solemn vow.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book VI, Canto XVIII. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
आनयैनं हरिश्रेष्ठ दत्तमस्याभयं मया ।
विभीषणो वा सुग्रीव यदि वा रावणः स्वयं ॥
content.transliteration:
ānayainaṃ hariśreṣṭha dattamasyābhayaṃ mayā |
vibhīṣaṇo vā sugrīva yadi vā rāvaṇaḥ svayam ||
content.text: Bring him here, O foremost among monkeys; sanctuary has been granted by me to him, whether he be Vibhishana or Ravana himself!
content.translation: Bring him here, O foremost among monkeys; sanctuary has been granted by me to him, whether he be Vibhishana or Ravana himself!
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book VI, Canto XVIII. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
ततो युद्धपरिश्रान्तं समरे चिन्तया स्थितम् ।
रावणं चाग्रतो दृष्ट्वा युद्धाय समुपस्थितम् ॥
content.transliteration:
tato yuddhaparīśrāntaṃ samare cintayā sthitam |
rāvaṇaṃ cāgrato dṛṣṭvā yuddhāya samupasthitam ||
content.text: Beholding Rama standing fatigued on the battlefield lost in contemplation, while Ravana stood before him eager for battle, the sage Agastya approached to impart the Aditya Hridaya.
content.translation: Beholding Rama standing fatigued on the battlefield lost in contemplation, while Ravana stood before him eager for battle, the sage Agastya approached to impart the Aditya Hridaya.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book VI, Canto CV. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.

content.sanskrit:
रामो रामो राम इति प्रजानामभवन् कथाः ।
रामभूतं जगदभूद् रामे राज्यं प्रशासति ॥
content.transliteration:
rāmo rāmo rāma iti prajānāmabhavan kathāḥ |
rāmabhūtaṃ jagadabhūd rāme rājyaṃ praśāsati ||
content.text: Rama, Rama, Rama alone was the joyful discourse of all the people; the entire world became imbued with righteousness while Rama ruled the realm.
content.translation: Rama, Rama, Rama alone was the joyful discourse of all the people; the entire world became imbued with righteousness while Rama ruled the realm.
content.provenance: Griffith (1870-1874), Book VI, Canto CXXVIII. Project Gutenberg #51540 (public domain). Sanskrit companion-only.
